items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1960-01-03
items.q: Harry James is an impresario. He heard me play, and he asked me if I could furnish him a band.

ctx.x: All right. Now, about when did you organize your first band?

Well, I was playing on a court here on Canal Street, and Harry James is an impresario. He heard me play, and he asked me if I could furnish him a band. So at this time, I used to play at the Old Haymarket, and they had several men playing that I knew, and we formed that band and brought that band to Chicago. And that was in March of 1916.

items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1958-05-26
items.q: And he approaches us and offers us $75 a week to play in the Casino Gardens.

ctx.x: What was his name again? Carter?

Earl Carter. Yeah. A Chicago drummer. He filled in for two weeks. And Spobara comes up and takes his place. This man knew that that's all the way we used him for two weeks. And we did pretty good at the Del Abbey. Then Harry James buys an entrance in the Casino Gardens with Aikenbar and Reeves. And he approaches us and offers us $75 a week to play in the Casino Gardens. We went and played the Casino Gardens. That was Kinzen Clock. And that band was Spobara. Nunes was still with us. And Edwards, Regas, and myself.…

items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1959-10-26
items.q: But the first time I ever heard it, when it was a first called out in front of the band, then Mr. James advertised us as a jazz band.

ctx.x: You don't know how far the word went back before that, though.

Oh, no. It could have been gone for years before I knew it. I wouldn't say that that was the first time it was used because I'd be telling a lie. I wouldn't know nothing about that. But the first time I ever heard it, when it was a first called out in front of the band, then Mr. James advertised us as a jazz band.

items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1958-06-09
items.q: I prefer that you interview Mr. Harry James by yourself because I believe that you are the lone person by asking him valuable questions about your common past.

ctx.x: Their champion was a colored man. Let's say a colored man has his rightful place in any music. Why not the white man to eulogize another man that hasn't created anything because of his color? That must be his music. But although Elvin Presley went on to hikes while the other guy stayed there, if you listen to his style, he couldn't have been original because he changed four or five different times. But fate is blind and can offer me a very next opportunity to go to the States for another film. I suppose you have well received my letter dated November the 11th that I have sent you from Calcutta.
